lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.indicator: Use place value to read and write numbers
lessons.provenance: NaCCA B7 indicator used in tests/test_curriculum_v2.py; exemplar record B7.1.1.1.1

excerpt.objective: Learners can Use place value to read and write numbers
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Number and Numeration Systems'). Perform the first step of Use place value to read and write numbers without explaining it and ask learners to predict what you will do next and why.

phase2.description: Teacher works through one fully-reasoned example of Use place value to read and write numbers on the board, thinking aloud so learners see the method and the reason for each step.
Read the text for Use place value to read and write numbers together, pausing to question and clarify; learners underline evidence relevant to the indicator.
Learners answer comprehension questions on Use place value to read and write numbers, giving evidence from the text rather than guessing.

learner_sample: Learn the key words for Use place value to read and write numbers and preview the text, predicting its content from the title.
Read the text for Use place value to read and write numbers together, underlining evidence relevant to the indicator.
excerpt.assessment: Comprehension questions on Use place value to read and write numbers requiring text evidence, plus oral reading for learners who struggle with writing. Success = Learner can produce original work applying the concept. Assessment mode: Comprehension questions or oral reading assessment.
excerpt.class_assignment: Learners read the passage on Use place value to read and write numbers and answer the comprehension questions, giving evidence from the text. The teacher checks the answers of three learners and corrects one common error.
excerpt.home_assignment: Read the text on Use place value to read and write numbers again and write three sentences about the main idea.
excerpt.conclusion: Ask learners to summarise Use place value to read and write numbers in their own words, emphasise the target language and set a short follow-up reading task. Preview the next lesson ('Use place value to read and write numbers').

lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.indicator: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction

excerpt.objective: Learners can Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Use place value to read and write numbers'). Tell a one-minute local scenario about Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction (a market, home or community situation) and ask: 'what would you do here, and why?'

phase2.description: Present a scenario, question or source about Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction and let learners identify the key issue involved.
In mixed-ability pairs, learners solve a parallel problem on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction. Move between pairs and correct any wrong step immediately.
Each learner solves two problems on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction alone, then the class analyses one common wrong answer and explains why it fails.

learner_sample: Follow the worked example for Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction on the board, noting each step and the reason for it.
In mixed-ability pairs, solve a parallel problem on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction, explaining each step to your partner.
excerpt.assessment: Written class exercise of 2-3 problems that test Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction; mark for correct method and correct answer. Success = Learner can correctly use the concept in a given situation. Assessment mode: Written problem-solving with step marks.
excerpt.class_assignment: In pairs, learners work through two problems on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction in their exercise books. The teacher moves round, checks each pair's method and asks one pair to explain their reasoning to the class.
excerpt.home_assignment: Write and solve three short problems of the same type as today's work on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction. Show each step clearly.
excerpt.conclusion: Two groups report their findings on Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction; the class agrees the strongest evidence and one open question.

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.indicator: Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases

excerpt.objective: Learners can Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases
excerpt.starter: Show a real object or a picture connected to Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases and ask learners to say three things they notice about it before any explanation.

phase2.description: Learners observe Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases closely and record exactly what they see or measure in a simple labelled table.
Learners sort/group the given items according to the rule for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases, explaining the basis of each group using .
Groups compare their evidence on Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases with the earlier prediction and agree one conclusion the evidence actually supports.

learner_sample: Examine the two contrasting examples for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases and identify what is the same and what is different.
Sort or group the given items by the rule for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases, explaining the basis of each group.
excerpt.assessment: A classification exercise on Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases: learners must sort items and justify each group. Success = Learner can explain or describe the concept in own words. Assessment mode: Classification exercise with accuracy check.
excerpt.class_assignment: Pairs sort or group the given items by the rule for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases and write one reason for each group. The teacher checks a sample and asks two pairs to justify a borderline item.
excerpt.home_assignment: Collect or draw five items you can group and write the rule you used to group them for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases.
excerpt.conclusion: Ask learners to state the rule or method for Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases in one sentence, then give one new example that fits it. Preview the next lesson ('Describe the characteristics of living things').

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.indicator: Describe the characteristics of living things

excerpt.objective: Learners can Describe the characteristics of living things
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Classify materials as solids, liquids and gases'). Ask learners to predict what will happen with Describe the characteristics of living things: record two or three predictions on the board without judging them yet.

phase2.description: In groups, learners carry out the fair test or activity for Describe the characteristics of living things, keep one condition constant and record every result honestly.
Learners observe Describe the characteristics of living things closely and record exactly what they see or measure in a simple labelled table.
Groups compare their evidence on Describe the characteristics of living things with the earlier prediction and agree one conclusion the evidence actually supports.

learner_sample: Watch and listen carefully, then describe each step of Describe the characteristics of living things in your own words.
Take an active part in the activity for Describe the characteristics of living things.
excerpt.assessment: Observe learners carrying out Describe the characteristics of living things using a short checklist, then ask them to explain their result in writing. Check that the explanation matches the evidence, not a memorised answer. Assessment mode: Oral questions and observation of participation.
excerpt.class_assignment: In groups, learners demonstrate the task for Describe the characteristics of living things while the teacher observes and records which learners have met the indicator.
excerpt.home_assignment: Practise the steps for Describe the characteristics of living things at home and be ready to show one step in the next lesson.
excerpt.conclusion: Ask the class to answer the question that opened the lesson about Describe the characteristics of living things, and to explain how their evidence supports the answer.

lessons.subject: English Language
lessons.indicator: Use formal and informal register in conversation

excerpt.objective: Learners can Use formal and informal register in conversation
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Speaking and Listening'). Build a quick word wall for Use formal and informal register in conversation: learners say the key words they already know, and the teacher adds the two they will need today.

phase2.description: Teacher reads the model text aloud, highlighting the target language feature for Use formal and informal register in conversation so learners both see and hear it in use.
Learners read the text and underline the evidence for Use formal and informal register in conversation, pausing to ask and answer questions.
Each learner completes and improves their piece on Use formal and informal register in conversation against a short checklist.

learner_sample: Watch and listen carefully, then describe each step of Use formal and informal register in conversation in your own words.
Complete the task for Use formal and informal register in conversation on your own and check your work before you finish.
excerpt.assessment: Assess the independent production task against a short checklist for Use formal and informal register in conversation. Also note oral contributions during guided practice for learners who struggle with writing. Assessment mode: Oral questions and observation of participation.
excerpt.class_assignment: In groups, learners demonstrate the task for Use formal and informal register in conversation while the teacher observes and records which learners have met the indicator.
excerpt.home_assignment: Practise the steps for Use formal and informal register in conversation at home and be ready to show one step in the next lesson.
excerpt.conclusion: Ask two learners to explain Use formal and informal register in conversation to the class in their own words, and ask one other learner whether they agree. Preview the next lesson ('Ask questions to elicit elaboration in conversation').

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.indicator: Distinguish between manual and automatic devices

excerpt.objective: Learners can Distinguish between manual and automatic devices
excerpt.topic: Introduction to Computing - Components of Computers and Computer Systems
excerpt.starter: Show a real object or a picture connected to Distinguish between manual and automatic devices and ask learners to say three things they notice about it before any explanation.

phase2.description: Learners sort devices, pictures or parts for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices into groups by how they work, and justify each group.
Present the second item and have learners note how it differs for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices.
Learners compare two devices or two ways of doing Distinguish between manual and automatic devices and state which is faster or more reliable and why.

learner_sample: Examine the first item for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices and note its features.
Examine the second item and note how it differs for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices.
excerpt.assessment: Mark the comparison chart for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices for accurate similarities and differences. Success = Learner can break down the concept and identify relationships. Assessment mode: Comparison chart or Venn diagram assessment.
excerpt.class_assignment: Learners complete a comparison chart for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices, listing the similarities and differences. The teacher checks three charts against the class model.
excerpt.home_assignment: Draw a table comparing two things related to Distinguish between manual and automatic devices and list one similarity and one difference.
excerpt.conclusion: Ask learners to state the rule or method for Distinguish between manual and automatic devices in one sentence, then give one new example that fits it. Preview the next lesson ('Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar').

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.indicator: Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar
lessons.provenance: Derived from exemplar record B7.1.1.2.1 learning focus + curriculum action verbs

excerpt.objective: Learners can Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar
excerpt.topic: Introduction to Computing - Windows and the Desktop
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Distinguish between manual and automatic devices'). Perform the first step of Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar without explaining it and ask learners to predict what you will do next and why.

phase2.description: Teacher demonstrates Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar on a real device or a labelled diagram, naming each part as it is used; learners observe the steps and the effect of each action.
Learners repeat or reproduce the demonstration for Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar with the teacher's prompts, using .
Learners perform the task for Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar on their own and check their work against the demonstrated steps.

learner_sample: Watch the demonstration of Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar and note each step and the reason for it.
Repeat or reproduce the demonstration for Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar with the teacher's prompts, using .
excerpt.assessment: Ask oral questions and set a short task that tests Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar. Success = Learner can correctly use the concept in a given situation. Assessment mode: Observation of practical performance with checklist.
resources: computer or projected screen where available
excerpt.class_assignment: In groups, learners demonstrate the task for Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar while the teacher observes and records which learners have met the indicator.
excerpt.home_assignment: Practise the steps for Demonstrate how to use the Start screen, tiles and taskbar at home and be ready to show one step in the next lesson.

lessons.subject: Creative Arts and Design
lessons.indicator: Create a simple pattern using local materials

excerpt.objective: Learners can Create a simple pattern using local materials
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Pattern and Decoration'). Perform the first step of Create a simple pattern using local materials without explaining it and ask learners to predict what you will do next and why.

phase2.description: Teacher demonstrates the technique for Create a simple pattern using local materials with locally available materials, naming each step and the tools used.
Learners carry out the practical task for Create a simple pattern using local materials in small groups using , with the teacher correcting technique.
Learners apply the discussion to a local situation, answering 'what would we do here?' about Create a simple pattern using local materials.

learner_sample: Watch the demonstration of Create a simple pattern using local materials and note the order of steps and the safety points.
Carry out the practical task for Create a simple pattern using local materials in your group using , following the demonstrated steps.
excerpt.assessment: Assess the finished product or process for Create a simple pattern using local materials against a short rubric (correct steps, safety, quality). Success = Learner can produce original work applying the concept. Assessment mode: Practical task assessment with rubric.
excerpt.class_assignment: In groups, learners carry out the practical task for Create a simple pattern using local materials, following the demonstrated steps. The teacher observes technique and safety and gives short corrective feedback as they work.
excerpt.home_assignment: Practise the steps for Create a simple pattern using local materials at home where it is safe to do so, and write down the steps you followed.
excerpt.conclusion: Three learners display or perform their work on Create a simple pattern using local materials; the class gives one kind, specific point of feedback each.

lessons.subject: Social Studies
lessons.indicator: Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy

excerpt.objective: Learners can Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy
excerpt.starter: Build on the previous lesson ('Energy Resources'). Tell a one-minute local scenario about Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy (a market, home or community situation) and ask: 'what would you do here, and why?'

phase2.description: Introduce the key words needed for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy and let learners preview the text, predicting its content from the title.
Learners break down the information for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy, identifying patterns, causes or relationships.
Learners investigate the case about Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy in groups, giving reasons and listening to other views before reporting.

learner_sample: Take an active part in the activity for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy.
Work with your partner/group to carry out the task for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy and record what you find.
excerpt.assessment: Ask oral questions and set a short written task requiring learners to give a reason for a view on Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy. Look for reasoning, not just recall. Assessment mode: Oral questions and observation of participation.
excerpt.class_assignment: In groups, learners demonstrate the task for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy while the teacher observes and records which learners have met the indicator.
excerpt.home_assignment: Practise the steps for Explain sources of energy in Ghana and ways of conserving energy at home and be ready to show one step in the next lesson.
